paragraphs.title: Keeping Away from the Holy Things and Guarding Their Holiness

easy.question: To whom did the Lord speak at the beginning of the passage?
answers: Moses
Aaron
The Israelites
easy.explanation: The first verse says, “The Lord spoke unto Moses.”

easy.question: To whom was Moses to deliver the command?
answers: The Israelites only
Aaron and his sons
The elders only
easy.explanation: The second verse tells Moses to speak to Aaron and his sons.

easy.question: What must not be done to the holy name?
answers: Mention it
Write it
Profane it
easy.explanation: The command is not to profane the Lord’s holy name.

medium.question: Why must Aaron and his sons be careful regarding the holy things?
answers: So they will not eat meat
So they will not profane the Lord’s name
So they will not serve in the Tabernacle
medium.explanation: They must keep away from the holy things so that the Lord’s name will not be profaned.

medium.question: What sequence of events is described in the passage?
answers: The Lord speaks to Moses, Moses commands Aaron and his sons, and a warning is given for future generations
Aaron speaks to the Lord, and then Moses commands the people
The Israelites dedicate holy things, and then the Lord speaks to Moses for the first time
medium.explanation: First the Lord addresses Moses; Moses then passes the command to Aaron and his sons, and the warning applies to future generations.

medium.question: In the phrase “separate themselves from the holy things,” what does “separate themselves” mean?
answers: Come closer
Decorate them
Keep away from them
medium.explanation: The phrase means to set oneself apart and keep away from the holy things.

challenge.question: What punishment is described for someone who approaches the holy things while unclean?
answers: He is sent into the wilderness
He loses his possessions
He is cut off from the Lord’s presence
challenge.explanation: The verse says that such a person “shall be cut off from my presence.”

challenge.question: What does the phrase “throughout your generations” show about the scope of the command?
answers: It applies only to Moses
It applies in every generation
It applies only on one particular day
challenge.explanation: “Throughout your generations” shows that the warning continues to apply to future generations.

challenge.question: What condition makes approaching the holy things a serious offense according to the verse?
answers: The person approaches while unclean
The person is not a descendant of Aaron
The holy things are outside the Tabernacle
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes the combination of approaching the holy things while uncleanness is upon the person.

questions.question: What punishment is described for someone who approaches the holy things while unclean?
answers: He is sent into the wilderness
He loses his possessions
He is cut off from the Lord’s presence
questions.explanation: The verse says that such a person “shall be cut off from my presence.”

questions.question: What does the phrase “throughout your generations” show about the scope of the command?
answers: It applies only to Moses
It applies in every generation
It applies only on one particular day
questions.explanation: “Throughout your generations” shows that the warning continues to apply to future generations.

questions.question: What condition makes approaching the holy things a serious offense according to the verse?
answers: The person approaches while unclean
The person is not a descendant of Aaron
The holy things are outside the Tabernacle
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes the combination of approaching the holy things while uncleanness is upon the person.

paragraphs.title: Uncleanness, Cleansing, and Eating the Holy Things

easy.question: Which descendant of Aaron may not eat the holy things until he is clean?
answers: One who has leprosy or a discharge
Anyone who serves in the Tabernacle
Only someone who is not a priest
easy.explanation: A descendant of Aaron with leprosy or a discharge may not eat the holy things until he is clean.

easy.question: What must someone who has become unclean do before eating the holy things?
answers: Offer a sacrifice immediately
Wash his flesh with water and wait until evening
Fast for a full day
easy.explanation: He remains unclean until evening and must wash his flesh with water before eating.

easy.question: Which foods may the priest not eat according to the passage?
answers: Bread and fruit
Fish and eggs
What died of itself or was torn by beasts
easy.explanation: The passage says that he may not eat what died of itself or was torn by beasts.

medium.question: What is the correct order after a descendant of Aaron becomes unclean?
answers: Eat, wash, and then wait until evening
Wash, wait until evening, and then eat the holy things
Wait a week, offer a sacrifice, and then eat
medium.explanation: He must first wash with water, wait until sunset, and only then eat the holy things.

medium.question: In the phrase “the person who has touched any such thing,” what does “person” refer to?
answers: A human being
An animal
A holy place
medium.explanation: Here the word refers to a human being who touched something unclean.

medium.question: When may an unclean descendant of Aaron eat the holy things?
answers: Immediately after touching the unclean thing
Only after offering a special sacrifice
After washing and after sunset
medium.explanation: The passage connects washing with water and the setting of the sun; afterward he is clean and may eat.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the passage’s treatment of uncleanness and eating the holy things?
answers: Every uncleanness permanently removes a priest’s right to eat holy things
Uncleanness prevents eating for a time, but after cleansing the priest may eat again
Only someone who is not descended from Aaron may eat holy things
challenge.explanation: The passage describes temporary uncleanness: after washing and sunset, the priest becomes clean and may eat again.

challenge.question: What serious result follows from failing to keep the Lord’s ordinance according to verse 9?
answers: The priest loses only his position
He must bring a grain offering
He bears guilt and may die because he profaned the holy things
challenge.explanation: The verse warns that anyone who fails to keep the ordinance bears guilt, and profaning it may lead to death.

challenge.question: How should the phrase “because it is his food” be understood regarding the holy things?
answers: The holy things are the priest’s allotted food, but he may eat them only when clean
The priest may eat any food even when unclean
The holy things are intended only for non-priests
challenge.explanation: The phrase shows that the holy things are the priest’s food, while the context makes eating them conditional on purity.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the passage’s treatment of uncleanness and eating the holy things?
answers: Every uncleanness permanently removes a priest’s right to eat holy things
Uncleanness prevents eating for a time, but after cleansing the priest may eat again
Only someone who is not descended from Aaron may eat holy things
questions.explanation: The passage describes temporary uncleanness: after washing and sunset, the priest becomes clean and may eat again.

questions.question: What serious result follows from failing to keep the Lord’s ordinance according to verse 9?
answers: The priest loses only his position
He must bring a grain offering
He bears guilt and may die because he profaned the holy things
questions.explanation: The verse warns that anyone who fails to keep the ordinance bears guilt, and profaning it may lead to death.

questions.question: How should the phrase “because it is his food” be understood regarding the holy things?
answers: The holy things are the priest’s allotted food, but he may eat them only when clean
The priest may eat any food even when unclean
The holy things are intended only for non-priests
questions.explanation: The phrase shows that the holy things are the priest’s food, while the context makes eating them conditional on purity.

paragraphs.title: Who May Eat the Holy Things

easy.question: Who may not eat a holy offering according to the passage?
answers: A stranger
A priest
One born in the priest’s household
easy.explanation: The passage says, “There shall no stranger eat of the holy thing.”

easy.question: Who may eat the priest’s food?
answers: Only his hired servant
A person bought with his money and one born in his household
Anyone from Israel
easy.explanation: A slave purchased by the priest and one born in his household may eat his food.

easy.question: What happens to a priest’s daughter when she marries a stranger?
answers: She eats more holy things
She becomes a priest
She may not eat from the holy offerings
easy.explanation: A priest’s daughter married to a stranger may not eat from the holy offerings.

medium.question: When may a priest’s daughter who married a stranger eat her father’s food again?
answers: If she is widowed or divorced and has no child
If she gives birth to a son
If her husband becomes a priest
medium.explanation: If she is widowed or divorced, has no child, and returns to her father’s house, she may eat his food again.

medium.question: In the phrase “one born in his household,” what does it mean?
answers: A guest in the priest’s house
Someone born in the priest’s household
A hired worker
medium.explanation: It refers to someone born in the priest’s household, who is included among those allowed to eat his food.

medium.question: What must someone do if he unknowingly eats a holy offering?
answers: Hide what happened
Return only what he ate
Add a fifth and give it to the priest with the holy thing
medium.explanation: He must add a fifth to the holy thing and give it to the priest.

challenge.question: What can be learned by comparing the priest’s hired servant with a person bought with his money?
answers: Not everyone who lives with the priest is allowed to eat holy things
Every worker in the priest’s house may eat holy things
Only a hired servant may eat holy things
challenge.explanation: A hired servant or temporary resident may not eat, but a purchased slave and one born in the household may; residence or work alone is not enough.

challenge.question: What change in the priest’s daughter’s status is described?
answers: She permanently ceases to be a priest’s daughter
Marriage to a stranger prevents her from eating, but returning to her father’s house may restore that right
She may eat only while married
challenge.explanation: Marriage to a stranger prevents her from eating, but if she becomes widowed or divorced without children and returns home, she may eat again.

challenge.question: Why does the passage emphasize that the holy things belong to the Lord and are sanctified by him?
answers: To teach that holy things are ordinary food
To allow everyone to eat them
To show that eating them unlawfully is a serious offense requiring special respect
challenge.explanation: The holy things are not ordinary property; they are sanctified to the Lord, so unauthorized eating brings guilt.

questions.question: What can be learned by comparing the priest’s hired servant with a person bought with his money?
answers: Not everyone who lives with the priest is allowed to eat holy things
Every worker in the priest’s house may eat holy things
Only a hired servant may eat holy things
questions.explanation: A hired servant or temporary resident may not eat, but a purchased slave and one born in the household may; residence or work alone is not enough.

questions.question: What change in the priest’s daughter’s status is described?
answers: She permanently ceases to be a priest’s daughter
Marriage to a stranger prevents her from eating, but returning to her father’s house may restore that right
She may eat only while married
questions.explanation: Marriage to a stranger prevents her from eating, but if she becomes widowed or divorced without children and returns home, she may eat again.

questions.question: Why does the passage emphasize that the holy things belong to the Lord and are sanctified by him?
answers: To teach that holy things are ordinary food
To allow everyone to eat them
To show that eating them unlawfully is a serious offense requiring special respect
questions.explanation: The holy things are not ordinary property; they are sanctified to the Lord, so unauthorized eating brings guilt.

easy.question: To whom did the Lord speak in verse 17?
answers: Moses
Aaron
All the Israelites
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The Lord spoke unto Moses.”

easy.question: To whom was Moses to speak in verse 18?
answers: The priests only
Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites
The strangers only
easy.explanation: Moses was told to speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites.

easy.question: What kind of offering is described in the verse?
answers: A peace offering
A sin offering
A burnt offering
easy.explanation: The verse says that the offering is to be made as a burnt offering to the Lord.

medium.question: Who may bring the offering according to the passage?
answers: Only the sons of Aaron
Anyone from Israel or a stranger living in Israel
Moses alone
medium.explanation: The passage includes both an Israelite and a stranger living in Israel.

medium.question: In the phrase “all their freewill offerings,” what is a freewill offering?
answers: A gift a person gives voluntarily
A punishment for sins
A priestly garment
medium.explanation: A freewill offering is a gift or sacrifice given voluntarily, unlike a vow, which is a commitment.

medium.question: What sequence of authority is described in the verses?
answers: The Israelites command Moses to speak to the Lord
Aaron commands Moses to speak to the Israelites
The Lord commands Moses, and Moses is to speak to the people
medium.explanation: The Lord first speaks to Moses, then commands him to address Aaron, his sons, and all Israel.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the passage also mentions the stranger living in Israel?
answers: The stranger is included in the instructions concerning offerings
The stranger may not approach the worship of the Lord
The stranger must be a priest
challenge.explanation: The passage explicitly includes the stranger living in Israel among those who may bring an offering.

challenge.question: What is the difference between a vow and a freewill offering?
answers: A vow is a commitment, while a freewill offering is given voluntarily
A vow is a required sacrifice, while a freewill offering is a prayer
There is no difference
challenge.explanation: A vow expresses a commitment, whereas a freewill offering is given voluntarily.

challenge.question: Why does the verse begin with “Any man, any man”?
answers: To say that only two men may offer sacrifices
To emphasize that every individual in the groups mentioned is included
To distinguish Moses from Aaron
challenge.explanation: The repeated wording emphasizes that every individual Israelite or stranger living in Israel is included.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the passage also mentions the stranger living in Israel?
answers: The stranger is included in the instructions concerning offerings
The stranger may not approach the worship of the Lord
The stranger must be a priest
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly includes the stranger living in Israel among those who may bring an offering.

questions.question: What is the difference between a vow and a freewill offering?
answers: A vow is a commitment, while a freewill offering is given voluntarily
A vow is a required sacrifice, while a freewill offering is a prayer
There is no difference
questions.explanation: A vow expresses a commitment, whereas a freewill offering is given voluntarily.

questions.question: Why does the verse begin with “Any man, any man”?
answers: To say that only two men may offer sacrifices
To emphasize that every individual in the groups mentioned is included
To distinguish Moses from Aaron
questions.explanation: The repeated wording emphasizes that every individual Israelite or stranger living in Israel is included.

easy.question: What animal is suitable for offering according to verse 19?
answers: A male without blemish
An animal with a defect
An injured female
easy.explanation: The offering must be a male without blemish from the cattle, sheep, or goats.

easy.question: What may not be offered according to verse 20?
answers: A young animal
An animal with a blemish
An animal from the cattle
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Whatsoever hath a blemish, that shall ye not offer.”

easy.question: Why might someone offer a peace offering according to verse 21?
answers: Only to eat the meat
To replace the priests
To fulfill a vow or bring a freewill offering
easy.explanation: The verse gives two reasons: to fulfill a vow or to bring a freewill offering.

medium.question: Why is an animal with a blemish not an acceptable offering?
answers: The offering must be perfect and without blemish
Animals may not be offered
Only birds may be offered
medium.explanation: The verses repeatedly emphasize that an acceptable offering must be perfect and without blemish.

medium.question: In the phrase “to accomplish his vow,” what does “accomplish” mean?
answers: Hide a vow
Fulfill a vow
Cancel a vow
medium.explanation: Here it means to fulfill or carry out a vow through the offering.

medium.question: What distinction does verse 23 make concerning an animal that has a superfluous or lacking part?
answers: It may be offered both for a vow and as a freewill offering
It may not be offered in any circumstance
It may be offered as a freewill offering, but not for a vow
medium.explanation: The verse says it may be offered as a freewill offering, but it will not be accepted for a vow.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from verse 25 about an offering received from a stranger?
answers: It must also be without blemish to be accepted
It may have a blemish
It is accepted only if it is a goat
challenge.explanation: The verse forbids offering an animal with a blemish even when it comes from a stranger; the requirement of wholeness remains.

challenge.question: What additional rule appears in verse 24?
answers: Meat may not be eaten in their land
Animals may not be injured in the ways listed
Offerings may not be brought from outside the land
challenge.explanation: The listed kinds of damage may not only be offered; they may not be inflicted on the animals in the land.

challenge.question: What does the repeated phrase “to be accepted” emphasize in verses 19–21?
answers: The offerer may choose any animal he wants
The offering is meant only for an ordinary meal
The offering must be suitable and acceptable before the Lord
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the offering must be acceptable before the Lord, which is why it must be perfect and without blemish.

questions.question: What can be inferred from verse 25 about an offering received from a stranger?
answers: It must also be without blemish to be accepted
It may have a blemish
It is accepted only if it is a goat
questions.explanation: The verse forbids offering an animal with a blemish even when it comes from a stranger; the requirement of wholeness remains.

questions.question: What additional rule appears in verse 24?
answers: Meat may not be eaten in their land
Animals may not be injured in the ways listed
Offerings may not be brought from outside the land
questions.explanation: The listed kinds of damage may not only be offered; they may not be inflicted on the animals in the land.

questions.question: What does the repeated phrase “to be accepted” emphasize in verses 19–21?
answers: The offerer may choose any animal he wants
The offering is meant only for an ordinary meal
The offering must be suitable and acceptable before the Lord
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the offering must be acceptable before the Lord, which is why it must be perfect and without blemish.

paragraphs.title: The Proper Time for Offering an Animal and Compassion

easy.question: Which animals are mentioned as suitable for an offering?
answers: A bull, a sheep, or a goat
A dove, a turtledove, or a lamb
A camel, a donkey, or a horse
easy.explanation: The verse mentions a bull, a sheep, and a goat.

easy.question: How many days must a newborn animal remain with its mother before it may be offered?
answers: One day
Seven days
Fourteen days
easy.explanation: It must remain under its mother for seven days; from the eighth day onward it may be offered.

easy.question: What may not be done on the same day?
answers: Feeding a mother and her young
Separating the young from its mother
Killing an animal and its young
easy.explanation: The verse forbids killing a cow or ewe and its young on the same day.

medium.question: Why may a newborn animal not be offered immediately?
answers: It must remain under its mother for seven days
Young animals may never be offered
It must be one year old
medium.explanation: The verse requires the newborn to remain under its mother for seven days; only from the eighth day is it suitable.

medium.question: In the phrase “from the eighth day and thenceforth it shall be accepted,” what does “accepted” mean?
answers: It will disappear
It will be suitable and accepted
It will run quickly
medium.explanation: In the context of an offering, “accepted” means suitable and acceptable before the Lord.

medium.question: What sequence is described in the verses?
answers: Slaughter, birth, and then seven days of waiting
Seven days under the mother, followed by the possibility of offering it from the eighth day
Offering on the first day, followed by time with the mother
medium.explanation: The young remains under its mother for seven days and may be offered from the eighth day onward.

challenge.question: If an animal was born on Sunday, what is the earliest day it may be offered?
answers: The following Sunday
Saturday of that same week
Monday of that same week
challenge.explanation: The day of birth counts as the first day, so the eighth day is the following Sunday.

challenge.question: What distinguishes verses 27 and 28?
answers: Verse 27 discusses only a bull, and verse 28 only a goat
Verse 27 concerns when the young becomes suitable for offering, while verse 28 forbids killing a mother and her young on the same day
Verse 27 concerns eating, and verse 28 concerns rest
challenge.explanation: Verse 27 establishes the proper time for an offering, while verse 28 adds the prohibition against killing a mother and her young on the same day.

challenge.question: Which pair of animals is explicitly mentioned in the prohibition “it and its young”?
answers: A bull or a sheep
A goat or a lamb
A dove or a turtledove
challenge.explanation: Verse 28 explicitly mentions a cow or ewe and its young.

questions.question: If an animal was born on Sunday, what is the earliest day it may be offered?
answers: The following Sunday
Saturday of that same week
Monday of that same week
questions.explanation: The day of birth counts as the first day, so the eighth day is the following Sunday.

questions.question: What distinguishes verses 27 and 28?
answers: Verse 27 discusses only a bull, and verse 28 only a goat
Verse 27 concerns when the young becomes suitable for offering, while verse 28 forbids killing a mother and her young on the same day
Verse 27 concerns eating, and verse 28 concerns rest
questions.explanation: Verse 27 establishes the proper time for an offering, while verse 28 adds the prohibition against killing a mother and her young on the same day.

questions.question: Which pair of animals is explicitly mentioned in the prohibition “it and its young”?
answers: A bull or a sheep
A goat or a lamb
A dove or a turtledove
questions.explanation: Verse 28 explicitly mentions a cow or ewe and its young.

paragraphs.title: The Thanksgiving Offering and Eating It on Time

easy.question: Which sacrifice is mentioned in the verse?
answers: A thanksgiving offering
A sin offering
A peace offering
easy.explanation: The verse begins, “When ye will offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving unto the Lord.”

easy.question: When should the offering be eaten?
answers: The next day
That same day
A week later
easy.explanation: The verse says, “On the same day it shall be eaten.”

easy.question: What must not be done with the offering?
answers: Offer it
Bless it
Leave any of it until morning
easy.explanation: The command is, “Ye shall leave none of it until the morrow.”

medium.question: What is the connection between eating the offering that same day and not leaving any until morning?
answers: Both commands require the offering to be eaten within a short time
The prohibition applies only to priests
It may be left if it is frozen
medium.explanation: The command to eat it that day means that none may remain until morning.

medium.question: What must happen first according to the order of the verses?
answers: The offering must be left until morning
The offering must be eaten that day
The thanksgiving offering must be sacrificed
medium.explanation: First the thanksgiving offering is made; afterward it must be eaten that same day.

medium.question: What does “leave none of it” mean in the context “until the morrow”?
answers: Do not leave any of it
Do not offer it
Do not bless it
medium.explanation: It means that none of the offering may be left after that day.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “offer it at your own will”?
answers: The offering must be made only at night
The offering has nothing to do with thanksgiving
The offering must be brought willingly and in an acceptable manner
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that the offering is to be made willingly and in a manner acceptable to the Lord.

challenge.question: What is the precise time until which the offering may not be left?
answers: Until morning
Until noon
Until the end of the week
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says that none may be left until morning.

challenge.question: Why does the verse end with “I am the Lord”?
answers: To identify who ate the offering
To emphasize that the command comes from the Lord
To say that the offering may be eaten only in Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the instruction to eat the offering that day is a divine command.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “offer it at your own will”?
answers: The offering must be made only at night
The offering has nothing to do with thanksgiving
The offering must be brought willingly and in an acceptable manner
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that the offering is to be made willingly and in a manner acceptable to the Lord.

questions.question: What is the precise time until which the offering may not be left?
answers: Until morning
Until noon
Until the end of the week
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says that none may be left until morning.

questions.question: Why does the verse end with “I am the Lord”?
answers: To identify who ate the offering
To emphasize that the command comes from the Lord
To say that the offering may be eaten only in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the instruction to eat the offering that day is a divine command.

easy.question: What does the Lord command the people to do?
answers: Keep his commandments and do them
Build a Tabernacle
Bring an offering
easy.explanation: The verse commands them to keep the commandments and carry them out.

easy.question: Who gives the command in the verse?
answers: Moses
The Lord
The priest
easy.explanation: The verse ends with “I am the Lord,” showing that the Lord gives the command.

easy.question: Which phrase describes carrying out the commandments?
answers: Ye shall keep
My commandments
And do them
easy.explanation: “And do them” refers to putting the commandments into practice.

medium.question: What is meant by “Ye shall keep my commandments, and do them”?
answers: It is enough to know the commandments without obeying them
One must both guard the commandments and carry them out
Only one commandment must be performed
medium.explanation: The verse mentions both preserving the commandments and putting them into practice.

medium.question: What does “ye shall keep” mean in this context?
answers: Forget my commandments
Speak about my commandments
Observe and obey my commandments
medium.explanation: In this context, “keep” means to observe and carefully obey the commandments.

medium.question: What does “do them” refer to?
answers: The commandments mentioned earlier
The sanctuary
The prophets
medium.explanation: “Them” refers back to “my commandments.”

challenge.question: What special emphasis comes from saying both “keep” and “do”?
answers: The commandments are meant only for thought
People may choose only some commandments
Faithfulness to the commandments must also be expressed through action
challenge.explanation: The wording stresses that an inward attitude is not enough; the commandments must also be carried out.

challenge.question: What can be learned from “my commandments” rather than simply “commandments”?
answers: The commandments belong to the Lord who gave them
The commandments belong only to priests
The commandments are merely suggestions
challenge.explanation: The possessive “my” identifies the commandments as the Lord’s commandments.

challenge.question: What is the function of “I am the Lord” at the end of the verse?
answers: To describe a particular place
To emphasize the authority of the one giving the command
To announce that the commandments have ended
challenge.explanation: The ending reminds the reader that the Lord is the one giving the command, which establishes its authority.

questions.question: What special emphasis comes from saying both “keep” and “do”?
answers: The commandments are meant only for thought
People may choose only some commandments
Faithfulness to the commandments must also be expressed through action
questions.explanation: The wording stresses that an inward attitude is not enough; the commandments must also be carried out.

questions.question: What can be learned from “my commandments” rather than simply “commandments”?
answers: The commandments belong to the Lord who gave them
The commandments belong only to priests
The commandments are merely suggestions
questions.explanation: The possessive “my” identifies the commandments as the Lord’s commandments.

questions.question: What is the function of “I am the Lord” at the end of the verse?
answers: To describe a particular place
To emphasize the authority of the one giving the command
To announce that the commandments have ended
questions.explanation: The ending reminds the reader that the Lord is the one giving the command, which establishes its authority.

easy.question: What must not be done according to the verse?
answers: Profane the Lord’s holy name
Eat among the Israelites
Sanctify the Israelites
easy.explanation: The verse commands, “Neither shall ye profane my holy name.”

easy.question: Where does the verse say that the Lord will be hallowed?
answers: Among the nations
Among the children of Israel
Only in the Tabernacle
easy.explanation: The verse says, “I will be hallowed among the children of Israel.”

easy.question: How does the Lord describe himself at the end of the verse?
answers: The one who saves Israel
The one who teaches Israel
The one who sanctifies Israel
easy.explanation: The verse says, “I am the Lord which hallow you.”

medium.question: What relationship exists between the two commands in the verse?
answers: The Lord’s name must not be profaned, and it must be hallowed
The Lord’s name must be profaned in order to sanctify Israel
There is no connection between profaning and holiness
medium.explanation: The verse places the prohibition against profaning the name alongside the command to hallow it.

medium.question: What does “profane” mean in the phrase “profane my holy name”?
answers: Keep it hidden
Treat it with contempt or violate its holiness
Speak it aloud
medium.explanation: To profane something holy is to treat it as though it were not holy, in contrast with hallowing it.

medium.question: What can be understood from the phrase “among the children of Israel”?
answers: Holiness belongs only to one location
Only the priests are commanded to hallow the name
Recognition of the Lord’s holiness must appear among the people of Israel
medium.explanation: The phrase shows that the Lord’s holiness is to be recognized within the community of Israel.

challenge.question: What does the contrast between “neither shall ye profane” and “I will be hallowed” teach?
answers: Profaning and hallowing are the same action
The actions of the Israelites can express opposite attitudes toward the Lord’s name
The Lord’s name is unrelated to human behavior
challenge.explanation: The verse presents two opposite possibilities: dishonoring the Lord’s name or leading others to recognize its holiness.

challenge.question: What is implied by the wording “I will be hallowed”?
